grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Present perfect with for and since
grammarPoints.rule: Use have/has + the past participle to talk about something that started in the past and is still true now. Use for with a length of time and since with a point in time when it started.
grammarPoints.pattern: subject + have/has + past participle + for / since + time

chart.title: Present perfect with for and since

intro_examples.text: Kitesurfing has been popular for about fifteen years.
intro_examples.jp: カイトサーフィンは約15年間ずっと人気があります。

intro_examples.text: Surfing and skateboarding have been popular since the 1970s.
intro_examples.jp: サーフィンとスケートボードは1970年代からずっと人気があります。

intro_examples.text: How long have you done extreme sports?
intro_examples.jp: どのくらいエクストリームスポーツをしていますか。

rows.jp: 彼らは2019年からずっと友達です。

rows.example: Kitesurfing has been popular for fifteen years.
rows.jp: カイトサーフィンは15年間ずっと人気があります。

rows.pattern: for + a month / five years / an hour
rows.example: I have played soccer for six years.
rows.jp: 私は6年間サッカーをしています。

rows.example: He has skied since he was born.
rows.jp: 彼は生まれたときからずっとスキーをしています。

rows.pattern: How long + have/has + subject + past participle?
rows.example: How long have you done extreme sports?
rows.jp: どのくらいエクストリームスポーツをしていますか。

chart.note_rule: The present perfect connects the past to now. The action or state started earlier and has not finished.
chart.note_exception: Use for with a length of time (for five years) and since with the moment it began (since 2019).
chart.note_exception_detail: Never use since with a length of time: say for an hour, not since an hour. Ask about the length with How long...?

notes: Contract have/has in speech: I've, you've, he's, she's, it's, we've, they've.
Make the negative with haven't / hasn't: I haven't skied since last winter.

grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Adverbs of emphasis
grammarPoints.rule: Put an adverb of emphasis — so, very, really, incredibly, extremely, super, totally — in front of an adjective to make it stronger.
grammarPoints.pattern: subject + be + adverb of emphasis + adjective

chart.title: Adverbs of emphasis

intro_examples.jp: スケートボードはとてもわくわくします。
あの技は信じられないほど怖いです。

intro_examples.text: This boy's helmet looks totally cool.
intro_examples.jp: この男の子のヘルメットは完全にかっこよく見えます。

rows.jp: スケートボードはとてもわくわくします。
スケートボードはとてもかっこいいです。
あの技は本当に危険です。
あの技は信じられないほど怖いです。

rows.example: Those knee pads look super silly.
rows.jp: あのひざあては超おかしく見えます。

chart.note_rule: The adverb goes in front of the adjective, never after it.
chart.note_exception: Look and seem work like be: Those knee pads look extremely cool.
chart.note_exception_detail: Incredibly, extremely and totally are stronger than very. Super is informal — use it with friends, not in a report.

table.title: Adverbs of emphasis
notes: Order is always adverb + adjective: incredibly scary, not scary incredibly.
Do not stack two emphasis adverbs: say really scary, not very really scary.
